look_here_first: SLENDER INDIANGRASS candidate: archived two source-labelled AWNED very CURVED heads provide good candidate recognition. Strongest published mature split from S. nutans is dense NON-RHIZOMATOUS base, mainly ONE-SIDED ARCHING panicle, and typically 25–40 mm often TWICE-bent awns vs S. nutans rhizomatous, commonly once-bent 2–15 mm awns. Measure a true awn with mm ruler and verify actual base; the images do not prove these measurements. East Texas native is not automatic Hays County nativity. Species-level and county-range HOLD preserved.

project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Do not infer project native status from statewide Texas nativity or transfer S. nutans county records.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Compared with yellow Indiangrass S. nutans, this source-labelled grass often has longer (~1–1½ inch) awns and looser more strongly arching heads and tends to be nonrhizomatous; S. nutans generally has a denser straight/golden panicle, shorter (~⅓–1 inch) awns and short rhizomes. Root/collar/spikelet details overlap and must be checked on mature vouchered material. Local native status of S. elliottii remains UNRESOLVED.

visual_comparison.title: Slender Indiangrass — two actual source observations, compare true S. nutans anatomy
visual_comparison.subtitle: Two physically archived source-labelled S. elliottii heads show arches/awns, and two verified but different species S. nutans anatomy examples. Taxon identification and target-zone hold retained.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: SLENDER INDIANGRASS CANDIDATE: warm-season perennial clump with an OPEN, ARCHING and relatively sparse panicle, usually 4–14 inches in mature southeastern treatments, with awned spikelets. Mature awns often 1–1½ inches, longer than typical yellow Indiangrass S. nutans (~⅓–1 inch), but color and arching alone overlap. Verify mature awn with mm/ruler scale, Sorghastrum fertile SESSILE spikelet plus NAKED sterile pedicel, and actual collar and perennial nonrhizomatous crown. Two genuine source-labelled photographs show awned CURVING heads, not those micro features. PROJECT TARGET-ZONE RANGE REMAINS UNRESOLVED; source determination needs independent voucher-level review.

visual_comparison.overlay_note:
Panels 1–2: source-labelled S. elliottii; panels 3–4: S. nutans (different species). This is a provisional species-identity learning comparison, NOT a county-native PASS. No invisible glume/ligule or awn-length arrows claimed.
Confirmation checklist (source: World Flora Online — Sorghastrum elliottii treatment): Photograph a mature awn with a millimeter ruler: the treatment describes 20–35 mm awns, bent twice and twisted below the second bend. Record the spikelet body separately from its awn; the treatment gives 5–7 mm spikelets. Include the plant base: absence of rhizomes supports the determination, but a detached seedhead cannot establish that character. Still provisional: Existing source-labelled head photos still lack those measured characters; no independent photo-ID clearance.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Identify slender indiangrass from the whole plant toward measured spikelets
steps: BEGIN gallery panel 8 index7 (Anne Parker, CC BY): real *S. elliottii* source species intact spikelets and their long attached awns immediately beside actual metal millimeter marks. Hairy spikelet outer surfaces seen, but the mature fertile lemma and each glume are NOT peeled apart.

Panel 5 index4: individual awns and spikelet bodies alongside a centimeter-marked rule with half-millimeter tick marks. Observe lengths and the curved dark shafts without inventing an exact bend count from one 2D angle.

Panels 6 and 7 (indices 5–6) true source photographed inner blade/sheath region shows a pale folded mouth/lip. Determine where true free ligule attaches on your own specimen; its length is NOT calibrated in these pictures.
Gallery panel 9 index8 gives exterior sheath/culm attachment, NOT a reproductive awn or root.
Gallery panel 10 index9 shows brown stem and folded green-brown sheath in field, no actual exposed underground rootstock.
Original photos indices 0–1 show two independent photographers' mature long curved awned heads but cannot conclusively determine county range or internal floral identities.

Gallery indices 2–3 are *S. nutans*, a DIFFERENT SPECIES: one collar/ligule region and one fertile spikelet macro. Do not use these as *S. elliottii* anatomical proof; they orient where to inspect corresponding species organs.
One separate CC0 source image of a comparatively broad open panicle is held for species/phenology photo audit and intentionally left out of main teaching gallery.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
field_id_short_tiles.short: Arching, mostly one-sided panicle; confirm rooted tuft and long twice-bent awns
field_id_short_tiles.details: Slender Indiangrass candidate: seek a loose, usually one-sided, arching flowering panicle on a dense warm-season perennial tuft. Two archived S. elliottii source-labelled photographs show curved awned heads but DO NOT independently prove species identity, crown architecture, or awn dimensions. Never identify by golden/brown color or an arch alone.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PROVISIONAL SOURCE-ID HOLD — REQUIRES VOUCHERED ANATOMY

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · TRACE THE ROOTSTOCK
field_id_short_tiles.short: Dense tuft without spreading rhizomes; contrast S. nutans
field_id_short_tiles.details: Inspect a connected mature plant from roots through flowering stem. The published southeastern key separates caespitose S. elliottii (no extended rhizomes) from rhizomatous S. nutans. A detached seedhead cannot establish rootstock type. No existing S. elliottii photo verifies an intact rooted crown, and an eastern record does not prove Hays County nativity.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · OPEN THE REAL COLLAR
field_id_short_tiles.short: Photograph the inner ligule membrane at 1-mm scale
field_id_short_tiles.details: Pull the blade away from its sheath on a vouchered S. elliottii stem and show the true free ligule margin and any lateral extensions with a 1-mm scale. Panel 3 depicts the collar of OTHER SPECIES S. nutans, not S. elliottii; it must never be used as direct proof of this taxon's ligule. No unsupported ligule-length cutoff is asserted.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · ISOLATE THE FERTILE SPIKELET
field_id_short_tiles.short: Spikelet body about 5–7 mm; check bare sterile pedicel
field_id_short_tiles.details: Published World Flora Online treatment reports S. elliottii spikelets about 5–7 mm long. At 10–20× photograph one intact sessile fertile spikelet with an adjacent reduced/naked sterile pedicel; then separate and label glumes and lemma, measuring each rather than inferring glume venation or length from the whole head. Panel 4 is S. nutans reproductive anatomy for COMPARISON ONLY.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · MEASURE THE COMPLETE LEMMA AWN
field_id_short_tiles.short: Usually 20–35 mm, twice bent and twisted below the second bend
field_id_short_tiles.details: The cited World Flora Online account describes mature awns about 20–35 mm, twice bent and twisted below the second bend; a regional Florida key gives typically 25–40 mm (sometimes shorter). S. nutans is commonly shorter and once bent, but ranges overlap. Measure at least three complete awns from lemma attachment to tip with a millimeter ruler; separately record body length and both bend locations. The existing two source-labelled head photos cannot certify these measurements or the lemma attachment.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · RULE OUT YELLOW INDIANGRASS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Compare rootstock, one-sided head and several measured mature awns together
field_id_short_tiles.details: S. nutans usually has rhizomes, a fuller often golden panicle, and shorter commonly once-bent awns; S. elliottii is described as caespitose with an arching often one-sided head and longer twice-bent awns. Color, curvature, and any one awn are not conclusive. Panels 3–4 are explicitly S. nutans, not new S. elliottii evidence. Keep species identity and project-county status unresolved until independently authenticated specimen evidence is available.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PROVISIONAL — SPECIES-ID AND RANGE HOLDS REMAIN
